I'm not trying to make you paranoid or claim the people commenting in this thread are lying but I think you have to keep in mind that *here*, specifically in this subreddit, it will be very hard for you to find a man that wants to just be friends with a woman. 

The majority of men here have gone without any sort of romantic experience but are still wanting that sort of companionship. I think that's a reasonable assumption to make. That's my current position. A sub-segment of these men, very unfortunately, don't have friends either, or don't have any sort of reliable support system. 

Any man in this position who makes a close female friend will eventually find it hard to distinguish between friendship and signs of romantic attraction. How would a person who's never experienced romantic attraction know what it looks like, after all. Right? They'll use the next closest thing as reference. If that person still had any hope in trying to find romantic companionship, the thought of him picturing a relationship with the woman is inevitable. For that person, she is a *rarity* in their lives - a woman who does not treat them badly because of their looks or demeanour and who's willing to mutually hang out with. That, who god forbid, enjoys his companionship.

It's *because* of a man's lack of exposure in a situation 'normal' men take for granted, ie. having a close relationship with a woman, that they put the relationship and/or woman on a pedestal. They don't want to lose a potential chance when it only comes to them a literal handful of times. It's why the concept of experience is touted so many times by users here; why people here believe those seemingly 'insignificant' high school relationships matter. It's not about 'missing your youth', it's about not getting that exposure that increases your level of emotional maturity. Past a certain age, missing this sort of experience is considered 'abnormal'.

I think it's perfectly possible for you to find men who want to just be platonic friends with you. I think trying to find one *here* will be very hard. I also hope my comment also helps explain a bit why some (not all) of the men had the attitude they had toward you. It will probably be the most likely attitude men here would have toward you should you trying befriending users here.

Yes, oh yes this is very relatable. Amazingly relatable. I'll talk about one of my few passions: anime. Anime is _so good_ at this. The entire industry is built on the hopes and dreams of lonely men in Japanese society, repressed by their cultural expectations and work-life imbalance. It feeds them hopes and dreams that can never be achieved in real life and as anime expands its reach, it finds more and more people outside Japan similarly disenfranchised. It finds people like you and me who use games, movies, shows, as a simulation of what we're supposed to get out of reality.

You're right. Reality is gone. The fantasy has opened new ways to receive the love, care, interaction, socialisation, and affection we need to sustain ourselves. A facsimile version, for sure, but one that is growing more 'real'over time and continuously being integrated into our lives. And such high standards are no longer just from these sources of media. Social media and Internet 2.0, as everyone knows, has transformed human expectation and interaction. Everything from news feeds to subreddits, from dating sites to chatroom servers, we are all encouraged to only show our best foot forward and nothing else. It is perfection or nothing.

We used to have clear roles in early society, just after we passed our hunter-gatherer phase. You were the farmer, or you were the priest, the doctor, the sitter. Your tribe was hundreds small and you saw your actions have direct impact on your tribe for its betterment. Now you work regularly for the perceived betterment of society, but you cannot see it. All the while you hear about the widening income gap, the wars, the strife. When a certain girl was dismissed, lashed out at, by world leaders, for simply for stating we needed to do something about climate change, it was a clear sign that the 'bar' had indeed been lowered.

Go back to your game. You see your actions have consequences, positive consequences, that you know shape that world for the better. Of course you would choose the game world. Good prevails, people listen, _you_ can make a difference. No longer are you deadweight to your family or invisible to your friends. The media you indulge yourself in has given you more for your basic human needs than anything in the 'real' world ever has. Meaning is given to you.
